stem:
A continuous random variable $X$ takes values from 0 to 6 only and has a probability distribution that is symmetrical.

Two values, $a$ and $b$, of $X$ are such that $\text{P}(a < X < b) = p$ and $\text{P}(b < X < 3) = \frac{13}{10}p$, where $p$ is a positive constant.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Find $\text{P}(b < X < 6 - a)$ in terms of $p$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem:
It is now given that the probability density function of $X$ is $\text{f}$, where

$$\text{f}(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{1}{36}(6x - x^2) & 0 \leqslant x \leqslant 6, \\ 0 & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}$$
parts.text: Given that $b = 2$ and $p = \frac{5}{27}$, find the value of $a$.
